text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- President Guntis Ulmanis leaves today for a two-week visit to the U.S., where he will receive an award from the Central and Eastern European Law Initiative. He will also visit the San Fransisco stock exchange.
- Latvia and the International Monetary Fund have reached a new standby agreement for 18 months.
- The cabinet decided to allocate 50,000 lats to repair the trucks used by fire departments and the rescue service.
- The Russian foreign ministry says it hopes the new Latvian government will change its policy toward the country's Russian-speaking minority.
- The cabinet has approved the agreement between Latvia and Sweden on visa-free travel which is due to be signed on August 4.
- During the first half of the 1997 the number of passengers passing through the Riga International Airport grew six percent compared with the same period last year.
